candidates.name: Malignant Mesothelioma
support_spans: multiple pleural thickenings and a marked effusion on the left side
Epithelioid solid formations with pseudopapillary structures
Immunoreactive for calretinin, AE1/AE3, D2-40, Wilms tumor protein 1
Neoplastic cells immunoreactive for calretinin, confirming mesothelial origin
candidates.why: The patient's presentation with pleural thickenings and effusion, along with the pathological findings of epithelioid solid formations and immunoreactivity for calretinin, are characteristic of malignant mesothelioma.

candidates.name: Metastatic Malignant Mesothelioma
support_spans: Nodular growth observed on the mid third of the tongue
Neoplastic subepithelial proliferation, consisting of epithelioid cells in the tongue
candidates.why: The appearance of a nodular growth on the tongue with microscopic findings consistent with mesothelial origin suggests metastasis of the primary disease.

candidates.name: Pleural Mesothelioma
support_spans: multiple pleural thickenings and marked effusion on the left side
Homozygous deletion of CDKN2A gene by fluorescent in-situ hybridization
candidates.why: The patient's initial presentation with pleural thickenings and effusion, along with the genetic finding of CDKN2A deletion, supports the diagnosis of Pleural Mesothelioma.
